Alex (ml): Heads up — I'm looking at onboarding 'Clover-7B-v2' for a quantization eval (INT8/4-bit) and some benchmark runs. Found a 'LICENSE.md' in the repo that mentions a non-commercial clause. Before we spend cycles: what checks do we need to clear to bring this into Redwood for internal evals and potential Dedicated/private offering?

Maria R: Good catch. We always need: model card, full license text, dataset provenance (train/validation sources), and any third-party TOU called out. Also check for attribution or no-derivatives clauses. If there's an NC (non-commercial) clause, hosted API is probably a no-go.

Jamal T: Quick checklist draft:
```
- grab LICENSE.md and model_card.json
- search repo for dataset attributions (look for "CC-" and "non-commercial")
- run basic evals on a dev node (no public access)
- flag for legal + privacy review
- add export-control assessment (EAR/ITAR)
```
I'll attach the script I used to pull license text: `curl -s $REPO/raw/main/LICENSE.md | sed -n '1,120p'`

Sofia (legal): Thanks for the ping. Short answers:
- Non-commercial (NC) license: prohibits offering as a commercial hosted product. It still may be used for internal research or Dedicated/private deployments if the customer's license allows, but we need written clarity.
- No-derivatives (ND): prevents fine-tuning or distribution of modified weights. That blocks offering quantized/specialized builds to customers.
- Attribution (BY): okay but we must include proper attribution in docs and marketing.
- Share-alike (SA) or viral copyleft: requires downstream artifacts to be licensed similarly — big red flag for hosted.

Sofia (legal): Concrete ask: attach the raw LICENSE.md, model card, and any dataset TOUs. If there's any clause with the word "commercial" or "research-only", we escalate. Also include the intended use (internal eval vs hosted API vs Dedicated). Provide who will request exception if needed.

onboarding-bot: Intake created: ML-ONBOARD-129 — https://redwood.internal/ops/onboard/ML-ONBOARD-129. Summary: Clover-7B-v2, quantization evals, potential Dedicated/private. Checklist state: "license_check_pending".

Alex (ml): Quick clarification: If we run quantized experiments only on our infra and never redistribute weights, is that still violating NC or ND? Trying to understand boundaries for initial benchmarks.

Sofia (legal): NC/ND are about rights to use and distribute the model, not file formats. Running the model internally for research/benchmarks can be allowed under some NC licenses if the repo explicitly permits research use — but many NC clauses prohibit commercial research. For safety:
- Do NOT expose the model via hosted API without explicit commercial license.
- Do NOT ship quantized weights or modified checkpoints to customers if ND present.
- If in doubt, treat as "internal eval only" until Legal signs off.

Maria R: Operational mitigation ideas:
- Run all bench jobs in a locked namespace with no external access and log everything.
- Keep weights on a gated bucket with strict ACLs.
- Add a required "license_approval" checkbox on onboarding ticket before any compute spins up.

Jamal T: Adding export-control note: some contributors disclaim export restrictions or mention data from restricted jurisdictions. We should have an "export_check" boolean in the intake that triggers Security review. Also: PII in training data triggers Privacy sign-off.

Sofia (legal): Agreed. Required sign-offs for this intake: Legal, Security (export control), Privacy (dataset PII), and ML Lead (model safety). Please attach the model card and dataset manifest to ML-ONBOARD-129.

Alex (ml): Will do — I'll add the license and model_card links to the ticket and mark the intake as "license_check_pending". If Legal OKs internal eval, we'll proceed with INT8 experiments in a dev-only cluster and won't create quantized artifacts for external use. :thumbsup:

Maria R: Thanks. When you add files, ping @Sofia (legal) in the ticket so it's routed correctly.

Sofia (legal): Ping me there and include the exact license text copy/pasted. If there's an upstream contact (author/email), include that too — we sometimes request commercial terms.
